title: tier-2 shipped code: transform, filter and dispatch one leaf shape against 0x142cc1610

unreachableBranches.why: The sink check on the filter-rejected path. This unit's fixture leaves ctx[0x20] null in every case, so the guard jumps and the push is never taken; the push itself (0x142cc1450) is verified by no unit yet, so a non-null sink would compare bytes this unit does not implement.

The `type == 3` arm of the id overwrite. The corpus is restricted to type 0 (sphere) and type 1 (capsule), the two per-type primitives that are verified; type 3 needs the mesh world the element's pointers describe, which this fixture does not build.
The `type == 4` arm of the id overwrite, for the same reason: type 4 dispatches to 0x142cd0ae0, which is unread.
The sink check on the hit path. Null sink in every case, so the guard jumps and the push is never taken.
The sink check on the no-hit path. Null sink in every case, so the guard jumps and the push is never taken.

notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-sim/src/collide.rs (shape_narrowphase), called by crates/ow-sim/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the collision_narrowphase entry.

The leaf is void and writes only its second argument, the hit quad, which is the record's +0x20 quad - so that quad is the compared channel. The sink (ctx[0x20]) is null, so the wrapper skips its push and the 0x40-byte hit record stays on its own frame.

Everything the leaf reaches through pointers lives in one arena blob: the record, the filter arguments, the entry array, both transform pools and all five per-type pools. Every pointer inside it is an absolute arena address and the probe translates it back by ARENA_BASE.

The corpus stays on type 0 (sphere) and type 1 (capsule) - the two per-type primitives that are verified - and walks the shape index, the pool index, both transform branches, the filter's three outcomes and hits against misses. Types 2 and 4+ are unread, so the emulator would run code there is nothing to compare against.
The callback slot points at 0x140c9f110 (the leaf that returns a zero quad) so the indirect call is a real call; with a null sink its return is discarded by the wrapper.
The 0x7ff7c7e30818 and 0x7ff7c80b1030 reads are the two copies of the squared-length epsilon the sphere and capsule paths use.
The 0x7ff7c87e5f40 read is the stack cookie (0x143ac5f40): the leaf has a frame cookie and ends with __security_check_cookie.
acknowledgedGaps: The type-3 mesh path is implemented in the same function but is not exercised here: mesh_sweep needs a MeshWorld, which the narrowphase must derive from the element's own absolute pointers at +0x20/+0x28/+0x30, and the fixture that would prove that path is not built yet.
Types 2 (0x142cd3c80) and 4+ (0x142cd0ae0) are unread, so the Rust reports Narrowphase::UnreadType for them instead of guessing. The practice range is entirely type 3.
The sink push (FUN_142cc1450) and the hit callback are outside this unit: the wrapper's observable output is the hit quad, and the sink is null so nothing is pushed.
